title: Oakview Bank - Data residency & compliance discovery
next_steps: Send SOC2/ISO and HIPAA attestation docs
Share VPC deployment diagram and network requirements
Schedule technical deep dive with infra team (week of 2026-03-09)
Provide pricing for Dedicated reserved capacity and estimate for 30-day pilot
action_items: Michael Tran: email SOC2 + HIPAA docs by 2026-03-05
Sara Li: prepare initial benchmark plan and sample RPS for pilot by 2026-03-09
Luis Gomez: share current infra diagram and data flow by 2026-03-06
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
summary: Discovery with Oakview Bank to map compliance constraints (GDPR/GLBA/HIPAA), evaluate Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, and align on pilot scope. Key asks: no EU egress for US customers, customer-managed keys, strict log retention controls and proof points (SOC2/HIPAA). Next step: share security docs and schedule deep dive.
transcript:
00:00 Tom Reynolds: okay everyone good to start? we got 45 minutes, thanks for fitting us in.
00:12 Michael Tran: yep thanks Tom, Michael from Redwood, i'll kick us off, sara and nina from our eng team are here to answer the infra questions. quick agenda: understand your compliance constraints, current infra, decide if hosted/dedicated/private fits, and next steps. sound good?
00:28 Tom Reynolds: yep that's perfect. Priya our CISO is on — Priya when helpful please jump in.
00:34 Priya Desai: hi all, thanks. main thing for us: data residency and auditability. Oakview has customers only in the US but we also have two branches in the EU that handle a small set of accounts, so we need guarantees about data locality and logging.
00:50 Michael Tran: understood. to clarify, are you looking for Redwood to keep data strictly in region, or are you asking about encryption key residency as well?
01:03 Priya Desai: both. logs, model inputs, embeddings, everything — we need to avoid EU egress for US customer data, and keys should be customer-managed ideally. also HIPAA rules apply to some of our health-related benefit accounts, and GLBA for banking records.
01:21 Sara Li: thanks. on that front we support three deployment modes: hosted API (fastest), dedicated reserved pools (isolated capacity in a region), and private (VPC/on-prem). Hosted typically stores data in our control plane unless you configure private routing, dedicated gives tenant isolation but still host-managed, private gives you the most control — VPC peering or on-prem with customer-managed KMS.
01:44 Luis Gomez: when you say hosted stores data in control plane, do you mean customer data can leave our VPC? we'd prefer not to have any plain-text payloads leave our environment.
01:56 Nina Patel: good question. in hosted for standard customers payloads traverse Redwood's control plane so logs and traces may be retained per our retention policy. we do offer options: short retention windows, redaction, and an enterprise setting where you can enable private network paths and customer-managed keys — but that tends to look more like our Private offering.
02:18 Tom Reynolds: for Oakview we need: 1) US-only residency for production customer data, 2) customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), 3) minimal telemetry/logging with options to disable sensitive fields, and 4) audit logs we can export to our SIEM. is that doable?
02:35 Sara Li: yes those are standard enterprise asks. dedicated in a US region with customer KMS integration fits the bill; Private (VPC) gives you full routing so data never traverses our public control plane. we can also support export of audit logs to your S3 or syslog.
02:50 Priya Desai: about keys — do you support AWS KMS external key (EKMS) or an HSM connector? we can't have Redwood hold the root keys.
03:02 Nina Patel: we support AWS KMS customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private; HSM integration for on-prem/private deployments is supported as a project. for hosted customers we offer envelope encryption but not customer KMS by default.
03:16 Hannah Lee: and on certification side: do you have SOC2 Type II, ISO27001, and HIPAA BAAs? we need copies for legal review.
03:26 Michael Tran: yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 attestations and we sign HIPAA BAAs for qualifying customers. i'll send the attestation docs and the BAA template after this call.
03:36 Priya Desai: retention windows for logs — our compliance wants logs kept for 7 years for certain financial events, but telemetry for debugging should be short lived. can you separate audit log retention from telemetry?
03:50 Sara Li: absolutely. audit logs we can push to your retention store (S3) with your lifecycle policies; telemetry/traces we can set to a short retention window (30-90 days) or disable. we also support field-level redaction on inputs and outputs.
04:08 Luis Gomez: network — what's the typical network setup for Dedicated? do we need peering, or can we do private link?
04:18 Nina Patel: Dedicated typically uses VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink depending on your preference and security posture. Private offering is VPC-hosted in your account or on-prem packaged. We'll share a diagram.
04:30 Tom Reynolds: any limitations on model performance if we use customer-managed keys or Private? like will latency increase or throughput drop?
04:38 Sara Li: there is a small overhead for TLS termination and key lookups with external KMS — usually single-digit ms per init and minimal per-token impact. the bigger driver of latency is the deployment topology and instance types. we can recommend GPU types and batching configs to hit your SLOs.
04:56 Priya Desai: GDPR question — if a EU subject requests deletion, can you purge data from backups and logs? we need proof of deletion across all copies.
05:08 Michael Tran: for Private and Dedicated we can honor deletion requests and provide attestation of deletion in your region; for hosted we have stricter constraints — we can redact and exclude but full deletion from backups may be subject to our retention policies. we'll get formal language in the docs.
05:27 Tom Reynolds: what about embedding storage — we want to ensure embeddings for PII are not retained. can we opt-out of embedding persistence?
05:35 Nina Patel: yes we have a configuration to disable embedding persistence; alternatively you can enable prefix/KV caching on your side or use stateless DTOs. we'll show options in the pilot plan.
05:48 Luis Gomez: audit logs export — do you push in real-time or batch? we want near-real-time for fraud signals.
05:56 Sara Li: we can stream audit events via Kinesis or Pub/Sub, or batch to S3. near real-time is supported via streaming to your SIEM.
06:06 Priya Desai: penetration testing and vulnerability disclosure — do you allow us to run pen tests and will you provide patch timelines?
06:16 Michael Tran: yes we have a vuln disclosure policy; for Dedicated and Private deployments you have more control. for hosted we coordinate a scheduled pentest window with our security team. we'll include policy links.
06:28 Tom Reynolds: cost consideration — if we choose dedicated, what's the lift to get started, and can we do a small pilot?
06:36 Sara Li: you can start with a small reserved pool (e.g., 1-2 GPU instances) for a 30-day pilot. we provide pilot pricing and then scale to reserved capacity. we'll provide pricing scenarios based on expected RPS and model choice.
06:48 Luis Gomez: for the pilot we'll want to run standard prompts and also a synthetic dataset with PHI-like content to validate redaction and privacy controls. is that okay?
06:56 Nina Patel: yes, we recommend a benchmark plan including synthetic PHI, latency and throughput targets, and quality checks. sara will draft that.
07:06 Hannah Lee: legal question: data subject to discovery or legal holds — can Redwood preserve state if required?
07:15 Michael Tran: yes we support legal hold snapshots for Dedicated and Private; hosted may have limitations. we'll document the preserve/restore capabilities.
07:26 Tom Reynolds: any known customers in banking with similar constraints? references would help accelerate procurement.
07:33 Michael Tran: we have multiple regional banks on Dedicated and Private; i'll share anonymized case studies and a reference from a mid-market bank that went through HIPAA and GLBA reviews.
07:44 Priya Desai: logging restrictions — can we disable collecting the full prompt client-side and only send a hashed ID for traceability?
07:53 Sara Li: yes you can minimize telemetry by hashing or tokenizing client-side; we also support client-side redaction and field-level allowlists.
08:05 Luis Gomez: operationally, who owns the model upgrades and rollouts in Dedicated? we need predictable behavior for rollbacks.
08:14 Nina Patel: the customer controls the rollout policy; we offer canary and automatic fallback policies. for Dedicated you pin model versions; for Private we can run upgrades on your schedule.
08:24 Tom Reynolds: regarding auditability, we need immutable audit trails and ability to export full event logs for a 7-year retention. is immutability supported?
08:34 Sara Li: we provide append-only audit logs and can push to your immutable store or WORM S3 bucket. we'll include architecture notes.
08:42 Priya Desai: encryption at rest — if we use customer-managed KMS, are snapshots encrypted with the same key?
08:50 Nina Patel: yes snapshots and backups can be encrypted with your KMS keys when configured on Dedicated/Private.
08:58 Tom Reynolds: okay this is helpful. can you walk through a sample timeline for pilot and enterprise onboarding?
09:04 Sara Li: typical timeline: week 0-1 sign BAA + security docs, week 2 initial infra setup (VPC peering or Private), week 3 pilot start (small pool), week 4 run benchmarks and compliance checks, week 5 review and expand or convert to reserved capacity. we can compress or extend depending on procurement.
09:26 Priya Desai: procurement will ask for risk items and mitigations — you mentioned field-level redaction, customer KMS, private routing, audit export, and pen-test policy. can you package that in a single deck?
09:39 Michael Tran: yes i'll assemble a security packet with attestation docs, deployment diagram, and our pen-test policy.
09:47 Luis Gomez: networking specifics — what ports, IP ranges, and NAT behaviors should our networking team expect?
09:54 Nina Patel: we'll share a detailed network runbook with required egress/ingress, IP ranges for peering, and PrivateLink endpoints.
10:03 Tom Reynolds: are there any regulatory blockers for doing this all in the US footprint?
10:09 Michael Tran: no major blockers; for certain EU-only customer records you'd need to ensure EU tenancy. for US-only it's straightforward with Dedicated or Private.
10:18 Priya Desai: as long as we have contractual guarantees about residency and key control we'll be comfortable.
10:24 Michael Tran: understood. quick recaps: Michael will send SOC2/ISO + BAA and security packet; Sara will send pilot benchmark and pricing; Nina will share network diagram; Luis will send infra diagram; and we'll schedule a deep-dive next week.
10:38 Tom Reynolds: sounds good. any final questions?
10:41 Hannah Lee: timeline for docs? legal needs them this week if possible.
10:45 Michael Tran: i'll send initial docs today and the full security packet by tomorrow.
10:50 Priya Desai: great. thanks everyone.
11:00 Michael Tran: thanks all, we'll follow up — talk soon.
11:10 End of call

Notes: transcript has occasional transcription noise; product names sometimes abbreviated or mis-typed (e.g., K-V cache, Redwood Console -> Redwood console).
